method.harness: _compute.py (PEP 723; uv run) on Python 3.14.4: stdlib zlib, lzma, compression.zstd; pinned wheels (see versions.packages); static binaries under /home/coder/compression-ref/bench/bin (FFmpeg n9.0.2 BtbN GPL build, libjxl 0.12.0 tools, oxipng 10.2.1), fetched and checked by /home/coder/compression-ref/bench/setup.sh
method.exactness: Sizes, ratios and quality scores are exact and deterministic for the pinned versions and inputs: generators are seeded, gzip members carry mtime 0, archives use fixed dates and owners, MP4/MKV are written with -fflags +bitexact. Timings are medians of repeated runs after a warm-up (the count is stated next to each), on a 2-CPU cgroup shared with other tenants; they are reported as tiers, with cgroup throttling recorded before and after each timed phase. Video encodes are timed once each, and three settings three times (median, determinism check).
method.units: MB = 10^6 bytes; ratio = original / compressed; saving_pct = 100 * (original - compressed) / original
method.private_data: none read (no ~/.claude or ~/.quirq file is opened); the doomfly audit log is used for sizes and ratios only
method.heavy_artefacts: /home/coder/compression-ref/bench (outside the publication): media in /home/coder/compression-ref/bench/media/what-each-file-wants, encodes and scratch in /home/coder/compression-ref/bench/tmp/what-each-file-wants

json.method: Every codec/level compresses every form of every corpus once (exact bytes, verified by decompression; zlib-ng and libdeflate gzip output is also decoded by the stdlib gzip module). Forms: on_disk = the file's bytes; pretty = json.dumps(obj, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False); default_dumps = json.dumps(obj) (Python's ', ' and ': ' separators, ensure_ascii=True); minified = separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False. Timings: api_records minified and pretty, one codec at a time on one thread, gc off; warm-up = one compression of the first 256 KiB; compression median of 7 runs (3 when one run exceeds 2 s), decompression median of 7. Speeds are MB/s of the uncompressed input, 3 significant figures, labelled with a tier because the CPU is shared. knee_minified: ratio gained and compression speed lost from one level to the next.

small.method: Per-document: each test document compressed alone (gzip member mtime 0; raw DEFLATE with no framing; brotli quality 5 and 11 with its built-in static dictionary; zstd frames with the default content-size flag on; '_lean' = content_size_flag, checksum_flag and dict_id_flag all 0). Dictionaries: compression.zstd.train_dict(train_docs, size) on the train split only, measured on the disjoint test split. Passing a ZstdDict directly loads it undigested on every call (costly, about a millisecond for 110 KB here); '_digested' passes zd.as_digested_dict, which the ZstdDict caches per level (the speed table shows the difference). Batching: N consecutive test documents joined by newlines per frame. ratio_total = sum raw / sum compressed; docs_grew counts compressed > raw.

logs.method: Block sweep: the file is cut into fixed-size byte blocks (the last one shorter), each compressed as an independent gzip member / zstd frame / xz stream with full headers; bytes = sum over blocks; 'whole' = the file as one block. Seekable: independent zstd frames of 64 KiB or 1 MiB plus a seek table in the zstd contrib seekable format (skippable frame, magic 0x184D2A5E; 8 bytes per frame; 9-byte footer with magic 0x8F92EAB1), written by this harness; 200 random 1 KiB reads (seed 99) are checked against the original; overhead is against one zstd frame of the whole file at the same level. zstd_3_window_log_check: the whole file at level 3 with window_log forced to each value (level 3's default for inputs over 256 KB is 21); it tests why 1 MiB blocks can beat one frame at level 3. The audit log's content is never stored.

images.method: Lossless: every result is decoded and compared pixel for pixel with the source (lossless_ok). Lossy: each photograph is encoded at every listed setting; the output is decoded (Pillow for JPEG/WebP/AVIF, djxl for JPEG XL) to PNG and scored against the source PNG with ssimulacra2. bytes_at_ssimulacra2: bytes at the target score, interpolated linearly in log(bytes) between the two neighbouring settings that bracket it; null = the sweep never reached that score. timing_contention.note: encoders use FFmpeg/encoder default threading on the 2-CPU cgroup; wall time tiers, CPU seconds recorded

video.method: Each encode: FFmpeg reads the 240-frame Y4M and writes MP4 (-an, -map_metadata -1, -fflags +bitexact, -pix_fmt yuv420p), encoder defaults otherwise (GOP, threads, tune). kbps = video packet bytes * 8 / 10 s. core_crf_grid marks the settings named in the brief; the others (x264 CRF 33, x265 CRF 36, SVT-AV1 CRF 55) were added so each curve has 4 points. BD-rate (derived from curves_vmaf_kbps): draft-ietf-netvc-testing-09 sec. 4.2 -- log10(kbps) against VMAF (mean), a piecewise cubic Hermite interpolating polynomial through each codec's 4 points, integrated over the overlapping VMAF interval with 1,000 samples and the trapezoidal rule; reported only when at least 3 points of each codec lie inside that interval. The classic VCEG-M33 single cubic is recorded beside it (comparison_vceg_m33_cubic) with a monotonicity flag: on this clip the x264 cubic bends backwards between VMAF 87 and 93 and overstates the savings. kbps_at_vmaf: log-linear interpolation between neighbouring points. encoder_settings_reported: what each encoder says it used (x264/x265 SEI options; SVT-AV1 banner). GOPs are encoder defaults and differ: x264/x265 keyint 250 (one GOP plus scene cuts in 240 frames), SVT-AV1 gop size 161 (a second keyframe). Encode time: one run each; x264 CRF 23, x265 CRF 28 and SVT-AV1 P8 CRF 35 three runs (median) with a byte-identity check across runs.
